entry.description: Distinguishing planar Brownian images of time sets and measures. The primary source reports: Troscheit reports mutual singularity of planar Brownian image laws for s-Frostman probability time measures on [0,1], with 0<s<1, when their normalized expected correlation profiles have a nonvanishing limsup difference, including the stated lattice versus non-lattice self-similar class under the open set condition and dimension restrictions. In a fixed-dimension two-contraction family, each parameter has finitely many possible exceptions, and sufficiently small dimensions give pairwise separation. Minkowski-neighborhood reconstruction transfers specified measure-law distinctions to compact image sets. Equal profiles need not identify the original measure. Direct AI connection: The primary paper says LLMs performed part of the two-contraction calculations and drafted much Lean code; the arguments and ideas are human-created, with some influence from formalization. Owner metadata names Claude and GPT6. Further checking: Establish which calculations and proof changes were AI contributions; audit profile asymptotics, mutual-singularity quantifiers, small-dimension restrictions and Minkowski reconstruction. The formalization proves renewal results only for the self-similar laws used, not the full cited renewal theorem. Author checks are not independent review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override. The general profile-separation theorem explicitly requires a common Frostman exponent 0<s<1; no unrestricted all-dimension or arbitrary-measure reconstruction claim is made.

The other headline waist theorems are established mathematics; the sharp intermediate-dimensional Hausdorff constant remains open.
